passage: Tutor's note, after the placement test results. Nine of the batch cleared the first round; Siddharth did not. At the notice board Siddharth read Pradeep's name, went very still, and said flatly, "Lucky, Pradeep barely revised." Later in my room Siddharth admitted, "There's a bitter knot in my stomach. For a minute I wanted to move Pradeep's notes off our shared desk. I didn't." I said the feeling can be noted without being obeyed. That evening Siddharth walked to Pradeep's room, said, "Congratulations, I mean it," and asked how Pradeep had practised the timed papers. Pradeep pulled out a chair and started explaining. Siddharth's face stayed tight, but the pen kept moving on the notepad.

qa.q: How many of the batch cleared the first round?
qa.a: Nine of the batch cleared the first round.

qa.q: What was Siddharth feeling at the notice board, and what shows it?
qa.a: A bitter, jealous knot. Siddharth went very still, spoke flatly about Pradeep, and later admitted wanting to move Pradeep's notes off the desk.

qa.q: What did Siddharth do that turned the feeling into something useful?
qa.a: Siddharth congratulated Pradeep anyway and asked how Pradeep had practised the timed papers, instead of turning to contempt or sabotage.

qa.q: What might it be like for Pradeep when Siddharth arrives with congratulations and a question?
qa.a: Pradeep may feel respected and glad to share, shown by pulling out a chair and starting to explain, and may not know how bitter Siddharth felt earlier.

grounding: Shows envy at peers passing easily, noted honestly, followed by congratulating them and asking what worked, not contempt or sabotage.

passage:
Results day at the coaching centre in Patna, and the hall was packed, hot, noisy. The bank exam list went up on the board. Parveen's roll number wasn't there. Ramesh's was. So were two others from her batch who, she thought bitterly, had barely studied.

A hard knot twisted in her stomach. Part of her wanted to say something sharp, to walk out without a word to Ramesh.

She noticed the feeling. Jealous, she told herself. Okay. That's what this is.

Then she pushed through the crowd. "Ramesh. Congratulations. Really." He looked surprised, and pleased.

"Can I ask you something? What did you do differently this time?"

"Mock tests every Sunday," he said. "And I stopped reading new books in the last month. Only revision." He hesitated. "Want to join our Sunday group?"

She said yes. The knot didn't vanish. But it loosened.

qa.q: What did Ramesh say he did every Sunday?
qa.a: Ramesh did mock tests every Sunday.

qa.q: What was Parveen feeling when she saw the list?
qa.a: Parveen felt a bitter, jealous knot in her stomach and wanted to say something sharp.

qa.q: What did Parveen do with her envy that helped?
qa.a: She named the feeling, congratulated Ramesh sincerely, and asked what worked for him, which got her an invitation to the Sunday group.

qa.q: How might Ramesh have felt when Parveen congratulated him?
qa.a: Ramesh looked surprised and pleased, perhaps having expected coldness, and felt comfortable enough to invite her to study.

grounding: The story shows a young woman jealous of peers who passed, noting the feeling, congratulating them anyway and asking what worked.

passage:
The placement list was pinned outside the training office of the Bengaluru engineering college, and Vaibhav's name was at the top: a product company, the one Kamal had wanted since first year. Kamal's name wasn't there at all.

Back in the hostel, Kamal felt something sour spread through his chest. Vaibhav had skipped half the lectures. Vaibhav had borrowed his notes. When their group chat lit up with congratulations, Kamal typed, "Lucky day, huh," then deleted it. He thought about not forwarding Vaibhav the alumni contacts he'd promised. Nobody would know.

He sat with that thought, and didn't like who it made him.

That evening he knocked on Vaibhav's door. "Congratulations. You earned it." Then, before he could lose his nerve: "How did you prepare for the technical round?"

Vaibhav grinned. "Honestly? Mock interviews with seniors, every night for a month. Want me to set one up for you?"

qa.q: Which company did Vaibhav get placed in?
qa.a: A product company, the one Kamal had wanted since first year.

qa.q: What was Kamal feeling when he saw the placement list?
qa.a: Kamal felt bitter and envious, something sour spreading through his chest.

qa.q: What harmful choice did Kamal nearly make, and what did he do instead?
qa.a: He nearly held back the alumni contacts he had promised; instead he congratulated Vaibhav and asked how he prepared.

qa.q: How might Vaibhav have felt when Kamal knocked?
qa.a: Vaibhav seemed happy and generous, glad to share what worked and offering to set up a mock interview.

grounding: The story shows a young man jealous of a peer's success, noticing the feeling, congratulating him and asking what worked instead of quiet sabotage.
